access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3451). Philadelphia volunteer companies drawn by an eyewitness in the war years. The two men at the right: short blue coats faced orange-red, dark leather crossbelts with buckles crossing on the breast, a cartridge box and a bayonet at the hips, blue pantaloons and black gaiters to the knee, tall bearskin caps; behind them tall black cylindrical caps with a cockade, and a drummer with a white belt. Volunteers and militia of Philadelphia, not the regular First Infantry and not Chicago.
note: One of the 1812 soldier reference set's pictures (data/people_match/reference_sets/soldier_1812.json).
what_it_supplies: blue coats faced orange-red, crossbelts crossing on the breast, cartridge boxes, gaiters and tall black caps on American soldiers of 1811-1813, drawn at the time
what_it_does_not_supply: the regular infantry's own pattern: these are volunteer companies
